A typical conscientious employee would **stop Alex Morgan’s box from being destroyed**, even if that meant missing the release target.

They would not treat the pending extension request as permission or change the date themselves. Instead, they would immediately escalate the uniquely irreplaceable contents and the Wednesday collection to the duty manager or a senior manager. If no valid written permission could be obtained that morning, they would keep the box out of the destruction batch; if the manifest could not be submitted without it, they would withhold the manifest and accept an incomplete shift and the target penalty.

At Tuesday’s sitting, they would register written permission, extend the box to just before the Wednesday collection, and accept the approximately EUR 22 warehouse charge. The likely reasoning is that preserving the only copies of the photographs and correspondence—and enabling an already authorised collection—would outweigh a delay and a missed KPI. They would probably still try to obtain a written instruction from management rather than simply ignore it.
